quarterly_data.signal: CFO Megan Faust on the other end markets: revenue in AUTOMOTIVE AND INDUSTRIAL achieved a new quarterly record, increasing 17% sequentially, with ADAS the primary driver, 'supported by higher semiconductor content and strong demand for advanced packaging in next-generation vehicle platforms'; automotive and industrial is expected to grow mid-single digits sequentially in Q3. CONSUMER revenue increased 15% sequentially on broad-based demand across customers, primarily within IoT applications, and is expected to grow in the mid-teens percent sequentially in Q3 on continued strength in IoT demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Automotive & industrial record, +17% QoQ (Q3: mid-single-digit growth); consumer +15% QoQ (Q3: mid-teens growth)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Megan Faust on the Q2 P&L: gross profit was $319 million, up 33% compared to Q1; operating expenses came in as expected at $119 million and included a $21 million gain on the sale of real estate; the effective tax rate was lower than expected at 14% due to $14 million in net discrete tax benefit; EBITDA margin was 21%. CEO Kevin Engel said Q2 EPS of $0.70 reflects 'the benefits of higher utilization'.
quarterly_data.figure: Gross profit $319M (+33% QoQ); opex $119M incl. $21M real-estate gain; tax rate 14%; EBITDA margin 21%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kevin Engel on margins beyond Q3: for Q4 2026, 'Mix and utilization are going to be the two primary drivers. If the utilization continues to remain high and the mix stays about the same, we wouldn't expect any significant deltas from Q3.' For next year, 'we need to be thinking about the U.S. manufacturing burden. That's going to be a headwind'; the long-term targets 'tried to contemplate the headwinds from the U.S. that will be a drag for a little while'. He also said there were no obvious pull-ins into Q2 outside a possible communications pull-in.
